title: SmartDIMM: In-Memory Acceleration of Upper Layer Protocols
problem: Accelerators for upper layer protocols are restricted to CPU and SmartNIC locations, limiting acceleration variety. At high network rates with stateful transport protocols, frequent DRAM accesses and SmartNIC-CPU synchronizations become a bottleneck, outweighing the benefits of conventional hardware acceleration for protocols operating primarily on DRAM data.
motivation: Accelerating upper layer protocols like encryption and compression in datacenters is critical for performance, but conventional accelerator placement approaches have fundamental limitations in handling DRAM-intensive workloads with high contention.
method: SmartDIMM embeds the accelerator directly in DRAM using Samsung's AxDIMM, enabling end-to-end offloading of encryption/decryption and compression operations on DRAM-resident data. By co-locating computation with data in memory, SmartDIMM eliminates expensive SmartNIC-CPU synchronizations that plague other offload configurations.
key_novelty: Placing upper layer protocol accelerators inside DRAM (using Samsung's AxDIMM) to operate directly on memory-resident data, eliminating costly SmartNIC-CPU synchronizations.
contributions: Identifies the opportunity for in-DRAM acceleration of upper layer protocols operating primarily on DRAM data under high cache contention
Prototypes SmartDIMM using Samsung's AxDIMM for end-to-end encryption/decryption and compression offloading
Demonstrates that DRAM-resident acceleration outperforms CPU, SmartNIC, and PCIe-based offload configurations

metrics.speedup: 21.0% to 10.28× higher requests per second vs CPU-based encryption/decompression

limitations: Power consumption, hardware cost, and generalizability to additional upper layer protocols not discussed.
